name: Pidgin Tukang Besi
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only Donohue 1996 'Some trade languages of insular South-East Asia and Irian Jaya' (doctype: minimal); no grammar or phonology exists

sources.note: States only 'A Tukang Besi pidgin is used in the area' with no citation beyond the Glottolog code; the penultimate-stress statement it gives is for the full language (cites Donohue 1999 IPA Handbook).

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 1994. Tukang Besi. Journal of the IPA 24(1): 39-41 (Illustration)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Full language only (penultimate stress, secondary stress every second syllable); no pidgin mentioned.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent pidgin / trade / simplified / contact: no mention of a Tukang Besi pidgin; nothing on the pidgin's stress (concerns dialects of the full language).

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 1995. The Tukang Besi language of southeast Sulawesi, Indonesia. PhD thesis, Australian National University (ANU Open Research handle 1885/136142)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only first-hand open mention of the pidgin found: sec. 1.1 Setting (p. 1) 'now that the use of pidgin Tukang Besi is dying out fast, as a result of the spread of local Malay dialects'; sec. 1.3.2 lists the name 'Pogau Daoa' as a 'trade language used in the market between people from different dialect groups' (p. 7). No structural description of the pidgin and nothing on its stress. Sec. 2.3.2 Stress assignment ('Stress is regularly assigned to the penultimate syllable of the word, and secondary stress is assigned to every second (phonetic) syllable preceding the stressed syllable') describes…

sources.note: Eight Donohue items on the full language (thesis 1995, pronominals 2009, voice 2001, dialectology 2000, covert word classes 2008, pronouns/clitics 2008); nothing on the pidgin.
